1.

This is the prosecution of accused persons namely Pradeep, Santosh, Joginder,
Uday, Twinkle and Sachin pursuant to charge sheet filed by Police Station Saket U/s 395/412/120B/34 Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) subsequent to the investigation carried out by them in FIR No. 81/10.
2.

Succinctly, the facts of the case are that on 27.03.2010, complainant Sh. Ravi Ranjan Kumar came to the police station, Saket and got recorded his complaint i.e.
Ex. PW9/A on which the present FIR was registered.

As per the complaint of Sh. Ravi Ranjan Kumar, he along with his friend Kunal Kumar were to appear in an interview in Bharat Electronics Limited, Kotdwar, and was waiting for the bus at the bus stand at about 05.00 AM in front of TB Hospital, Lado Sarai.
2-3 more persons were standing there and waiting for the bus.
In the meantime, one white colour Scorpio car came in which five persons were sitting.
Out of the said persons, one asked about the way to Old Delhi Railway Station.
One of the person who was waiting for the bus stated that he knew the way to Old Delhi Railway station and he got into the car.
Complainant and his friend also asked the driver of the said Scorpio car that they also have to go to Old Delhi Railway Station.
So, they were also asked to sit in the car.
After 1km of distance travelled, the persons in the car stated that they are from crime branch and from the ATM machine Rs. 3.5 lakhs has been robbed.

Complainant and his friend were asked to submit their belongings including cash and ATM cards and stated that checking is going on and the complainant and his friend gave all cash,
ATM card and their Pan Card to them and also told the PIN of their cards to them.
It is further stated that after sometime, the accused persons made the complainant and his friend alighted from the car at Akshardham temple at around 7.00 AM.
The accused persons kept the ATM card, laptop, bag mobile phone, Rs. 1,500/- and documents of complainant and cash of Rs. 500/-, mobile phone and ATM cards of his friend with them.
By that time, the complainant and his friend came to know that they were looted.
On the basis of his complaint, the present FIR no. 81/10 was registered.
3. During the investigation accused persons namely Pradeep, Santosh, Joginder and Uday were arrested and recovery of the case property was effected.
Statements of the witnesses were recorded.

After the conclusion of the investigation carried out in the present case, police filed the charge sheet against the above mentioned accused persons for commission of offences U/s 395/412/120B/34 IPC.

STATEMENT OF ACCUSED PERSONS U/S 313 Cr.P.C.:
37.
Statement of accused persons recorded U/s 313 Cr.P.C in which all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence were put to them.

It is stated by accused persons that they are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
Accused persons opted not to lead any defence evidence.

ARGUMENTS:
38.
Ld. Additional PP for State has argued that prosecution witnesses have supported the case of prosecution and their testimony has remained unrebutted.
It is further argued that accused persons have been duly identified by the star witnesses and the recovery made from the accused persons have also been established on record.
That on a combined reading of testimony of prosecution witnesses, offences U/s 395/412 IPC are proved against the accused persons and u/s 174A IPC against the accused Sachin beyond reasonable doubt.

State vs Pradeep Etc (5) on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23324608/
8 39.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsels for accused persons have stated that there is no legally sustainable evidence against the accused persons.
It is argued that the accused persons have been falsely implicated in this case and no recovery has been effected from their possession and the recovery shown is actually planted upon them.
It is further submitted that the identity of the accused persons also could not be established beyond reasonable doubt.

Thus, on the aforesaid grounds the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt,
hence, the accused persons deserves to be acquitted.
FINDINGS:
40.
Arguments adduced by Ld. Additional PP for State and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused persons have been heard.
Evidences and documents on record perused carefully.
I have bestowed my thoughtful consideration to the rival submissions made before me.
Accused persons are indicted for the offences u/s 395/412 IPC and u/s 174A IPC.

After appreciating the evidence and going through the testimony of the prosecution witnesses this Court finds the accused persons not guilty for any offence charged herein and they deserves acquittal for the following reasons:-
41. Prosecution has examined two star witnesses namely PW7 Kunal Kumar and PW9 Ravi Ranjan Kumar being the victims in this case.
At the outset, it is to be noted that none of the above witness has identified accused Joginder, Uday and Sachin during their deposition recorded before the court.
Now coming to the testimony of the star witnesses of the prosecution one by one.
42. PW7 Kunal Kumar during his examination in chief stated that he could not see the robbers as his head was down when they were robbed so he could not identify the accused persons.
PW7 further stated that he could not even identify accused Pradeep (since PO) if he was present in the court.
As this witness did not support the case of the prosecution as far as identity of the accused persons is concerned, he was cross examined by Ld.
Additional PP for the state.

42.1 During cross examination, PW7 admitted his signatures on the arrest memos and personal search memos of accused Santosh, Pradeep (since PO) and Joginder exhibited as Ex. PW4/E to Ex.
PW4/I, however, he stated that the police officials obtained his signatures on blank papers.
42.2 Further, during his cross examination he admitted his signatures on the seizure memo of ATM card Ex. PW4/L but denied the suggestion of it being recovered from the accused Pradeep (since PO).
PW7 categorically denied the suggestion put to him by the Ld.
Additional PP for the state regarding the role of the accused persons and their identity.

State vs Pradeep Etc (5) on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23324608/
9 42.3
During cross examination of PW7 by the accused, it is admitted by PW7 that his mother while applying for new ATM card had informed the bank that previous ATM card was lost.
This admission of PW1 contradicts the case of the prosecution about the robbing of his ATM card.

42.4 PW7 in his examination in chief nowhere deposed about the recovery of robbed articles from the accused persons though as per prosecution he was with police team when accused persons got effected the recovery of robbed articles from their houses.
Thus, in view of the discussion above, the testimony of PW7 is found to be contradictory and inconsistent, therefore, does not inspire the confidence of the court.
Above all, the identity of the accused persons by the PW7 could not be established.
43. Now coming to the testimony of PW9 Ravi Ranjan Kumar.
There are material contradictions and inconsistencies appearing in his testimony that renders it to be shaky and unreliable.
There are discrepancies in his version vis-a-vis the testimony of other victim i.e. PW7 Kunal Kumar which also creates cloud of doubt in the story of prosecution.

43.1 At the outset it is to be noted PW9 has not identified the accused Santosh with certainty and stated that he could only identify accused Pradeep (since PO) amongst the 2-3 persons who were apprehended from the Esteem Car.
PW9 has also failed to identify the other accused persons as the perpetrator of crime in this case.

43.2 Further, initially PW9 stated in his examination in chief that the police recovered his laptop,
ATM card and mobile phone from the house of accused persons and in the subsequent part of the examination in chief he stated that he do not remember exactly from whose house his ATM card and mobile was recovered and stated that his laptop was sold by the accused persons and from some shop it was recovered by the police.
Apparently, the aforesaid statements of PW9 are contradictory in nature.

43.3 Further, PW9 in his examination in chief admitted his signatures on the seizure memo of Lenovo Laptop as Ex. PW9/C and claimed the recovery happened in his presence whereas during his cross examination by the accused, PW9 admitted that police has not taken him to any shop from where laptop was recovered and further admitted that all the papers bearing his signatures were prepared in the police station by the IO.

Now this admission by the accused during cross examination creates strong doubt in the manner of preparing of seizure memo and the recovery of the robbed articles itself which demolishes the story of prosecution.
43.4 Further, during the cross examination of PW9 he has admitted that he has seen the accused Pradeep (since PO) for the first time in the police station Saket.
He further admitted that police informed him that accused persons in this case have been apprehended.
PW9 could not tell when accused Pradeep (since PO) was arrested in this case.

This admission on the part of the PW9 again contradicts his own version in the examination in chief regarding the apprehension of the accused Pradeep (Since PO) and creates strong doubt in the story of the prosecution as a whole.

State vs Pradeep Etc (5) on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23324608/
10 43.5 PW9 in his examination in chief was put the case property i.e. laptop bag on which words HCL was engraved claimed by the prosecution to be robbed articles, however, the witness PW9 stated that the said laptop bag does not belong to him.
Hence, this recovery shown to have been effected by the prosecution does not get connected in the commission of the offence in question.
43.6 PW9 has not stated in his examination in chief the date of recovery of articles effected from the accused persons and on which date he joined the police team for recovery proceedings.

Further,
PW9 during his cross examination stated that Xylo car was not seized in his presence and he has seen the same in police station which is contrary to the story of prosecution as per which the car was seized in presence of PW9 who stood as witness to seizure memo Ex. PW13/8.

43.7 The discrepancies and the contradictions discussed above in the testimony of PW9 are material enough to demolish the veracity of his testimony and it cannot be given due credence to be relied upon.
It does not inspire confidence of the court to act upon.
44. Prosecution has examined PW2 Jayant Kumar Jaiswal who produced Xylo car before the police and police seized the same.

As per police, the Xylo car was driven by accused Santosh but PW2 has nowhere stated in his deposition that accused Santosh was driving the vehicle bearing no.
DL12CA0184 on 27.03.2010 when the incident took place.
Further, as per PW7 and PW9 it was white scorpio in which they took lift and in which incident happened so here also the story of prosecution becomes doubtful with respect to vehicle used in offence.
45. As per the case of prosecution, some currency notes of denomination of Rs. 500/- were recovered from the house of accused Santosh , Joginder and Pradeep (since PO).
PW4 Ct. Mast Ram has been examined by prosecution as the recovery witness to the same.

First and foremost there is no identification or distinguishable mark on the currency notes recovered from the accused persons that connects or proves to be same currency notes that have been robbed from the victims.

Secondly,
no independent public witness has been joined at the time of recovery of the currency notes by the IO.
During cross examination, PW4 has admitted that parents of accused Pradeep (since PO) were present at his home whereas the seizure memo Ex. PW4/Q does not bear the signature of either of the parent.
PW4 further admitted during cross examination that IO did not call any respectable person of the locality to be joined as independent public witness to the recovery proceedings.
None of the seizure memo Ex. PW4/S, Ex. PW4/R and Ex. PW4/Q bears the signatures of any independent public witness.

PW4 during cross examination at one place stated that IO has asked public persons to join the investigation but none agreed and IO even tried to serve notice to the public persons present there to join the investigation but they refuse to receive the notice and join the investigation whereas this fact is not corroborated by the testimony of IO PW13 SI Ajay Tyagi.
He nowhere in his deposition stated to have made efforts to join the independent public witness at the time of recovery proceedings.
Non joining of public witnesses also causes a dent in credibility of prosecution version.

In this regard reliance is being placed on the case law reported as "Anoop Joshi Vs. State" 1992(2) C.C. Cases 314(HC) in which High Court of Delhi had observed as under:
"18.

entities.text: Anoop Joshi Vs. State" 1992(2) C.C. Cases 314(HC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is repeatedly laid down by this Court in such cases it should be shown by the police that sincere efforts have been made to join independent witnesses.

In the State vs Pradeep Etc (5) on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23324608/
11 present case, it is evidence that no such sincere efforts have been made, particularly when we find that shops were open and one or two shop-keepers could have been persuaded to join the raiding party to witness the recovery being made from the appellant.

In case any of the shopkeepers had declined to join the raiding party, the police could have later on taken legal action against such shopkeepers because they could not have escaped the rigors of law while declining to perform their legal duty to assist the police in investigation as a citizen, which is an offence under the IPC".
46. Thus, in view of the discussion above, the recovery of the currency notes from the house of the accused persons at their instance cannot be said to have been proved beyond reasonable doubt.
47. There is another glaring material variation in the testimony of PW7 and PW9 vis-a-viz the details of incident apart from the one that have already been discussed in previous paragraphs.

As per the examination in chief of PW7 there were already 5 persons in the cab when it reached at the bus stop who came out and asked about the route of Old Delhi Railway Station whereas PW4 in his chief stated that only two persons were sitting in the cab in front side when the cab arrived at the spot.
Further, PW9 stated that two persons already standing at bus stop sat with them in cab whereas it is not so stated by PW7 in his deposition.
As per PW9 the cab driver travelled at the distance of about 500 mtr and got one by stander sit in the cab which is also missing in the version of PW7.
The discrepancy above also create doubt on the presence and involvement of 5 persons in the incident.
48. As per Section 395 IPC, the requirement of 5 or more persons is must to attract this provision which is not fulfilled in this case by any cogent evidence lead on record.
Now if the offence us/ 395 IPC is not proved the offence u/s 412 IPC also cannot be said to be made out.

Even in this case,
recovery of robbed articles also could not be proved beyond reasonable doubt, therefore offence u/s 412 IPC is also not proved against the accused persons.

49. As far as offence charged against the accused Sachin u/s 174A IPC, is concerned this Court is of the view that the offence is not made out in view of the reports and the documents pertaining to the execution of the process u/s 82 Cr.P.C. Vide order dated 05.06.2010
, the Court of Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate concerned ordered the issuance of process u/s 82 Cr.P.C. and directed the matter to be put up on 30.07.2010.
It is pertinent to note that there is no time of appearance mentioned in the process Ex. PX-2 so as to enable and inform the accused to appear at a particular time.
The record reveals that the matter was not taken up on 30.07.2010.

The matter was taken up on 09.08.2010 i.e.
Ex. PW11/2 whereby the order sheet does not reflect marking of absence of accused Sachin before declaring the accused as proclaimed offender.

As per the rules and the law the process server was supposed to take the photographs of the proceedings pasted on the door of the house of the accused Sachin but in the instant case no photograph was taken.
No statement of anyone was recorded by the process server.

Hence, this court has reached to the conclusion that proper opportunity was not afforded to accused Sachin to appear on a particular date and time before the Court not the process u/s 82 Cr.P.C. was duly executed.
and thus he has been wrongly declared as proclaimed offender.
Accordingly, the offence u/s 174A IPC is also not proved qua the accused Sachin.

State vs Pradeep Etc (5) on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23324608/
12 50.
It is a settled proposition of criminal law that prosecution is supposed to prove its case on judicial file beyond reasonable doubt by leading reliable, cogent and convincing evidence.
The burden of proof of the version of the prosecution in a criminal trial throughout the trial is on the prosecution and it never shifts on to the accused.

Also it is a settled proposition of criminal law that accused is entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt if any in the prosecution story and such reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal.
51. In view of the material discrepancies in the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, this Court is of the view that prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

Neither the identification of the accused persons have been established as the assailants beyond reasonable doubt nor the recovery effected from their possession has been established beyond any tinge of doubt.
The story of prosecution remained under cloud of doubts.
Therefore, the accused persons are entitled to be given benefit of doubt.
Accordingly, accused persons namely Joginder, Santosh, Uday and Sachin stands acquitted of the charges levelled against them in the present case.
